cards.card: Mashreq Aura World Elite Credit Card

note: The main banks, chosen as the best-known large card issuers (no central bank ranking was read): First Abu Dhabi Bank, Emirates NBD and Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank. Emirates NBD's pages and its card documents (its credit card key facts and fees PDFs, on emiratesnbd.com and cdn.emiratesnbd.com) and ADCB's pages answered this research with a Cloudflare block on 2026-10-30 and weren't read, so Mashreq, the next large card issuer, is written in their place; Dubai Islamic Bank's covered cards (its key facts statement, August 2026) were looked at but not written: their profit is charged each month on the whole limit under a Salam contract, less a profit paid on the unused limit and a discretionary rebate, which the game's card form doesn't hold. First Abu Dhabi Bank's credit card fees, charges and finance rates (the sheet linked from each card's page, with a card replacement fee changed from 20 August 2026), read in full: every card on sale is written with its annual fee for the primary card, inclusive of VAT (none where it says Free; the FAB Z card's 105 dirhams waived for its first year); every card bears 3.99% a month on purchases and on cash; the cash advance fee is up to 3.15% plus VAT or 157.50 dirhams, whichever is higher, written at its top with VAT at the 5% the bank's schedule adds (3.3075%); the international transaction fee is up to 2.61% plus VAT and the scheme's charges, written as 2.7405% (the scheme's own charge isn't modelled), and 0% on the Travel and Z cards; the late payment fee is 241.50 and the over-limit fee 303.18 dirhams. The bank's general schedule of charges (updated July 2026) gives the minimum monthly payment, 5% of the outstanding balance or 100 dirhams, whichever is higher, and the returned cheque fee, 220.50; its over-limit fee there is 302.40, the card sheet's 303.18 being the later and the one written. Neither states a grace period (only a payment due date 21 to 25 days after the statement). The cards not on sale (up to 2,000 dirhams a year), the instalment and balance-transfer fees, credit shield, replacement, statement and letter charges aren't written: a holder meets them only by asking. Mashreq's key facts sheet for its credit cards (KFS_Cards_09 2026), read in full: each card's recurring annual fee for the primary card, VAT inclusive (none where it is free for life); a retail and a cash interest rate of 46.20% a year (the bank prices each holder dynamically and shows the actual rate on the statement; 46.20% is the only figure it gives, and its example uses 3.85% a month); a spread of 2.89% on international transactions, in dirhams or another currency (the scheme's charges on top aren't modelled); a cash advance fee of 3.15% or 210 dirhams, whichever is higher; a late payment fee of 241.50 and an over-limit fee of 303.45; and up to 57 days of interest-free credit on purchases, written as the grace. The sheet states the minimum payment only in an example (50 on 1,000), which isn't written as a rule. The Aura World card was first read on its own page on 2026-10-29 (500 dirhams plus VAT, 525, and 3.85% a month); the sheet keeps the fee and states the rate as 46.20% a year, the figure now written.
